author: Thomas Broyer <t.broyer@ltgt.net>
commit message:
Move from AMD and CommonJS to ES6 modules

With the exception of configuration, this is an almost-entirely
automated process:

    npm install amd-to-es6 esnext
    # Unname AMD modules
    sed -i "s|define.'[^']*'\s*,\s*|define(|g" \
        $(git grep --name-only  -e "define[(]'[^']*'\s*,")
    # Convert AMD modules to ES6 modules
    amdtoes6 -d src/ -o src/ -b
    # Convert CommonJS modules to ES6 modules
    find src/ -type f -name "*.js" \
        -not -name "*.min.js" -not -name "optimer_regular.js" \
        -exec esnext -I -w modules.commonjs {} \;
    # JS-Beautify output
    find src/ -type f -name "*.js" \
        -not -name "*.min.js" -not -name "optimer_regular.js" \
        -exec js-beautify -n -r {} \;
    # Remove dependencies
    npm uninstall amd-to-es6 esnext

Manual changes afterwards involved removing unused imports (ESLint
chokes on them as 'unused-vars') and re-formatting a number using
scientific notation that js-beautify broke in Core/Math/CVML.js.

commit message:
Limit command cancelation to refinement commands

The current implementation of BrowseTree and NodeProcess create a dead end if
initial imagery/elevation textures are canceled.

NodeProcess keeps the parent displayed until the children are ready, and
BrowseTree doesn't call NodeProcess.SSE on the children because the parent
is displayed.
So if one of the children's initial command is canceled, NodeProcess will never
issue new commands because it'll never process these children nodes and the
parent will be stuck forever with childrenLoaded() returning false.

Limit NodeProcess.SSE complexity

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
commit message:
refactor(core): rework texture update process

The main goal of this PR is to ease the usage of the texture update features of
itowns with objects that aren't TileMesh/LayeredMaterial.

One example of such situation is: being able to colorise a pointcloud using
a WMS server.

First the color and texture update mechanism have been splitted, since they don't
share that much code (yet).

Second, part of the update code has been moved back to the Provider and it helps
clarify the roles. Basically, the update loop has now no knowledge at all of
the internal logic of the behavior.

On the other hand the provider now directly implement the various update strategies,
since they're the only one capable of applying them to their protocol.

So the update process is now this;
   1. update code asks the provider if it wants to download new textures
   2. the provider returns the extents/url of the said textures
   3. the update code forward these commands to the scheduler
   4. when the command resolve, the update code process the result
(until now, the responsability of step 1/2 was shared between update/providers)

This also opens the way for a nice pattern: if at step 2 the provider returns the
full url the scheduler can directly check if the cache already has this resource
available and skip the whole queue/priority mechanism and improve the latency.

commit message:
fix(core): handle near pos. in box3 visibility functions

Projection matrix produces strange results when projecting a point behind
the camera near plane.
To avoid errors this commits clamp z coordinate to camera.near in camera space,
before projecting.

author: pierre-eric <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
commit message:
refactor(core): unify SSE computation methods

Until this commit each geometry type had its own SSE computation methods.
The goal of this commit is to provide a single method based on:
  - bounding-box (BB)
  - geometricError (in meters)
  - distance

The computation is simple:
  - transform camera in BB's basis
  - compute distance camera - BB
  - project geometricError on screen at distance

The last step produce a screen-space-error in pixels.

Geometric error values depend on the data type:
  - 3dtiles: the tileset defines a geometricError per node so we can use this value
  - pointcloud: PotreeConverter defines a spacing, which is the average distance
between points in each node. We use: geometricError = spacing / 2^depth
  - tiles: this commit adapted the existing formula to use consistent units

commit message:
feat(style): add Style inheritance

It is now possible to specify a `Style` parent for another `Style`. That
way, it is possible to define a global `Style` for a `ColorLayer`, while
defining one with property specific to a `FeatureGeometry` for example.
The `Style` of the `FeatureGeometry` will then only have the minimum
requirement, and it will read missing properties from its parent. It is
a dynamic reading, so it the parent values are changing, it is changing
as well for the child style.

This is a proposition for improvement in #1318.

BREAKING CHANGE: `Style#text.halo` is not available anymore, and each
property of it as been place in the `text` object, with the `halo`
prefix: `haloWidth`, `haloColor` and `haloBlur`.

commit message:
feature: add StaticProvider to download from a list of predefined images

Allows to use iTowns features without the trouble of setting up a WM(T)S server.

Given a metadata json file like this:

{
  'file1.png': [west1, east1, south1, north1],
  'file2.png': [west2, east2, south2, north2],
  ...
  'fileN.png': [westN, eastN, southN, northN]
}

The StaticProvider will simply find the best image for a given tile (= the image
with the smallest extent covering all of the tile's extent).

commit message:
Build using webpack, getting dependencies with NPM

Notable changes:
 * Replace src/ThirdParty/ entirely with NPM dependencies
 * Replace many src/Renderer/Three/ and src/Renderer/ThreeExtented
   scripts with scripts coming right from the Three.js module.
   Those are a bit hackish though, as they modify the THREE object;
   use with care.
 * Make all implicit dependencies on Three.js explicit by adding a

        var THREE = require('three');

   at the top of the files, or adding 'three' to the AMD dependencies.
 * Add aliases in Webpack to avoid rewriting many dependencies.
   Cleanup will be done in a forthcoming change.
 * Replace require-text with Webpack's raw-loader. This is configured
   as a rule for all *.glsl files, rather than on each import.
 * src/Renderer/Utils.js won't work as it "depends" on a "Cartography"
   module that doesn't exist. The import has been moved to the top of
   the file, but commented out so that Webpack doesn't complain.

commit message:
Implement different layer update strategies

Add a configuration option to specify what kind of update strategy
is applied for a given level.

This commits implements 4:
  * STRATEGY_MIN_NETWORK_TRAFFIC: minimize network traffic by always
fetching the texture level matching node's level. This is the default
strategy.
  * STRATEGY_GROUP: maps level to groups. This effectively reduces the
granularity of a given layer. Was previously implemented in TileMesh
for elevation.
  * PROGRESSIVE: this strategy progressively refine level. Increment is
configurable (default: 1)
  * DICHOTOMY: is a special case of PROGRESSIVE.

commit message:
Limit command cancelation to refinement commands

The current implementation of BrowseTree and NodeProcess create a dead end if
initial imagery/elevation textures are canceled.

NodeProcess keeps the parent displayed until the children are ready, and
BrowseTree doesn't call NodeProcess.SSE on the children because the parent
is displayed.
So if one of the children's initial command is canceled, NodeProcess will never
issue new commands because it'll never process these children nodes and the
parent will be stuck forever with childrenLoaded() returning false.

Limit NodeProcess.SSE complexity

author: Sam Scolari <56174573+Sam-Scolari@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Passing an non-null empty string into sourc.style gets overridden to "normal"

I am working with WMTS data from NASA and I ran into an issue where I needed to either pass &STYLE= into the api request or just leave it out as the tile set I am working with does not have a style. However, WMTSSource only checks whether source.style length is > 0.  If source.style is null or "" then it passes &STYLE=normal into the api request. Furthermore, simply not passing source.style a value passes &STYLE="normal" into the api request as well. WMTSSource must check whether source.style is null or an empty string or else setting source.style = "" will just be overridden to "normal" and therefore pass &STYLE=normal into the api request.

This solution should ensure that existing code that does not set source.style will continue to pass "normal" as the default assuming source.style is initialized as null. 

*This is my first ever pull request so forgive me if I'm missing something

author: Augustin Trancart <augustin.trancart@oslandia.com>
commit message:
Chore: Use babel to inline glsl file using webpack loader

As we need to inline glsl files for packaging, but *without* bundling
them like webpack does, we just deal with glsl inlining with babel
instead of webpack when building our lib folder. We need a way to tell
babel where and how to process these glsl though, and that's where
babel-plugin-webpack-loaders comes into play.

We still let webpack deal with glsl files when building our bundles, or
when using webpack-dev-server, hence the custom babel config in
webpack.config.js

commit message:
feat(core): add vector tile loading in TMS

Vector tiles can be loaded in TMS as textures. Only Mapbox Vector Tile
is supported for now. This commit adds a new Parser (VectorTileParser),
and a new Helper (similar to OGCWebServiceHelper) VectorTileHelper.

Modifications have been done in Feature2Texture to support style as a
function, and as an object.

Also add two examples showing the use of Mapbox Vector Tiles in iTowns.
The first one is loading a full vector tile layer in a Planar view,
while the second only display national parks on top of a simple Ortho
layer in a a Globe view.

author: Augustin Trancart <augustin.trancart@oslandia.com>
commit message:
chore(build): drop babel-plugin-webpack-loader

babel-plugin-webpack-loader allowed to use webpack loaders in babel to
transpile our sources. This commit changes the approach:
- it lets babel deals with ES6 modules when it runs alone
- it uses babel-plugin-inline-import to import json and glsl (this was
  done by webpack raw-loader before)

The consequence of that is that glsl and json are now handled by babel
instead of webpack. I believe this won't change anything.

We have now a slightly more complex webpack.config.js, but we removed
some copy-pasta and some magic, leading to a simpler config overall.

The fact we no more pass through webpack at each babel invocation gives
us some nice perf improvement:
- `npm run transpile` execution time is divided by 2 on my machine
- `npm run test-unit` execution time divided by 3.

commit message:
feat(parser): add partial z support for geojson parsing

According to RFC 7946 [1], we can have coordinates set as [lon, lat] but
also as [lon, lat, alt] in a geojson file. When parsing a geojson to
provide features, this wasn't respected and the z coordinates was always
set to 1. While this default value is not customizable yet, it is a
small improvement.

Unit tests for geojson have been added to reflect this change.

[1]: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7946#section-9

commit message:
fix (controls): add an offset after mouse movement

When moving the globe using GlobeControls, there was some kind of
offset, the globe not staying right under the cursor. This is visible if
the container of the canvas is not occupying the full page, the
container has a CSS position property different of the default 'static'
and there are elements right before it on the page, like the geoportal
case.

The solution to avoid this, is to detect the position of the container
and add an offset according to this position, using the
getBoundingClientRect method of the container.

commit message:
Implement different layer update strategies

Add a configuration option to specify what kind of update strategy
is applied for a given level.

This commits implements 4:
  * STRATEGY_MIN_NETWORK_TRAFFIC: minimize network traffic by always
fetching the texture level matching node's level. This is the default
strategy.
  * STRATEGY_GROUP: maps level to groups. This effectively reduces the
granularity of a given layer. Was previously implemented in TileMesh
for elevation.

author: Adrien <adrien.berthet@ign.fr>
commit message:
fix(source): set the Style.minzoom correctly in VectorTilesSource (#1395)

The previous behavior was as follow:
- check the presence of `minzoom` for a specific layer
- if it is not present, use `2` has a default value
- insert this value to the `stops` array
The resulting problem is that if `minzoom` is not defined and the first
`stop` value was greater than 2, it was still adding a `2 to first stop`
step.

A solution has been added here, to consider that the `minzoom` is either
the specified minzoom, or whichever is the highest between 2 and the
littlest `stop`.

author: Augustin Trancart <augustin.trancart@oslandia.com>
commit message:
chore(build): drop babel-plugin-webpack-loader

babel-plugin-webpack-loader allowed to use webpack loaders in babel to
transpile our sources. This commit changes the approach:
- it lets babel deals with ES6 modules when it runs alone
- it uses babel-plugin-inline-import to import json and glsl (this was
  done by webpack raw-loader before)

The consequence of that is that glsl and json are now handled by babel
instead of webpack. I believe this won't change anything.

We have now a slightly more complex webpack.config.js, but we removed
some copy-pasta and some magic, leading to a simpler config overall.

This also allows us to remove BABEL_DISABLE_CACHE=1 env var required by
babel-plugin-webpack-loader. That and the fact we no more pass through
webpack at each babel invocation gives us some nice perf improvement:
- `npm run transpile` execution time is divided by 2 on my machine
- `npm run test-unit` execution time divided by 10.

feature: allow layer custom 'can this tile get a better texture' mechanism

The default mechanism is based on a simple approach: if texture.level and
node.level don't match -> try to fetch a new texture.

This works well for providers that can compute meaningful level attributes,
but breaks if it's not possible.

This commit allows layer to have their own function.

author: Jack Lovell <jacklovell1990@gmail.com>
commit message:
Update notes and scripts for building wheels

Wheels for Python 3.7 to 3.9 can be built using manylinux2010, as
there are binary wheels of oldest-supported-numpy available for these
versions. For 3.10 onwards manylinux2014 is required for numpy binary
wheels. Building numpy from source in the manylinux containers is not
viable.

There are now two scripts, one for each manylinux version, which will
build wheels for all upstream-supported Python versions. These can be
run as-is: info is in the first few lines of these files. Also, the
dev notes on building wheels wtih manylinux have been updated to
reference these files.

author: Lovell, Jack J <Jack.Lovell@ukaea.uk>
commit message:
Add functions for max, min and peak-to-peak values of memoryviews

The Python built-in min() and max() functions are very slow on
memoryviews, and Numpy's min and max are also slow when called many
times on small memoryviews (e.g. coordinate arrays). This commit adds
functions which operate at the C level to quickly calculate the max,
min and peak-to-peak values of a memoryview to a 1D array of type
double.

author: cnlpepper <cnlpepper@4bf6d682-d48d-4364-819c-41f39e07019b>
commit message:
Refactored optical package to remove Wavebands.
Spectrum is now always a sequence of regularly spaced samples between a specified minimum and maximum wavelength.
While the Waveband approach was the most general it provided a lot of scope for mistakes - duplicate and overlapping Wavebands are possible.
A significant speed impact also occurs when interpolating/integrating Spectrum objects as it is not possibe to quickly identify the Waveband that contains the requested wavelengths (no bisection for instance).
The use cases for the Waveband approach are limited, hence the decision to simpify the code and remove them.

author: Lovell, Jack J <Jack.Lovell@ukaea.uk>
commit message:
Propagate exceptions in worker processes to caller

Ensure that exceptions in worker processes do not cause the entire
program to hang. The consumer process in the Multicore engine expects
every task to put something in the results queue, so we either put the
result itself (if the task ran without error) or the exception raised
by the task. This means the consumer is never stuck waiting for
results in the queue which will never arrive. A calling program can
catch the resulting RuntimeError if any of the workers fails, and deal
with it accordingly.

author: Lovell, Jack J <Jack.Lovell@ukaea.uk>
commit message:
Enable use of Raysect in interactive Jupyter notebooks

When using the `%matplotlib notebook` magic in Jupyter (iPython)
notebooks, the `pause()` function is not implemented. This causes
Matplotlib to raise an error when observations are made using
certain pipelines (RGB, bayer, spectral and mono pipelines).

However, the `pause()` function is only called to work around a lack
of live updating in the Matplotlib QT backend. This workaround is
not needed in the notebook backend, so can be skipped.

author: cnlpepper <cnlpepper@4bf6d682-d48d-4364-819c-41f39e07019b>
commit message:
Refactored optical package to remove Wavebands.
Spectrum is now always a sequence of regularly spaced samples between a specified minimum and maximum wavelength.
While the Waveband approach was the most general it provided a lot of scope for mistakes - duplicate and overlapping Wavebands are possible.
A significant speed impact also occurs when interpolating/integrating Spectrum objects as it is not possibe to quickly identify the Waveband that contains the requested wavelengths (no bisection for instance).
The use cases for the Waveband approach are limited, hence the decision to simpify the code and remove them.

author: Jack Lovell <jacklovell1990@gmail.com>
commit message:
Implement MPIEngine render engine

This render engine uses SPMD (single process, multiple data) to
perform renders in parallel, using MPI (message passing
interface). The paradigm is that multiple independent processes are
launched, all of which build their own copy of the scenegraph in
parallel and all generate rendering tasks. Each process with rank > 0
then works on a subset of those tasks and sends the results to the
rank = 0 process, which processes the results. After the render is
complete, only process 0 has the complete results.

MPI communications are blocking (send/recv rather than isend/irecv)
and use mpi4py's methods for general Python objects, rather than the
high performance equivalents utilising the buffer
protocol (Send/Recv). The latter is done to avoid loss of generality
of the render engine: it supports any function supported by the other
render engines, not just ones returning objects supporting the buffer
protocol. The use of blocking comms simplifies the implementation and
in testing (using the MPI variant of the raysect logo demo) the MPI
comms were a small fraction - < 5% - of the total run time, with the
vast majority of the time - > 85 % - spent in the render function
itself. So the simplicity of implementation does not have a
significant performance cost.

Tasks are distributed approximately equally among all workers at
startup, with no adaptive scheduling. Again, this is done for
simplicity of implementation as an adaptive scheduler would need some
way of tracking how long each process was spending on tasks and all
processes would need to communicate with one another about which tasks
they were taking on. Adding an adaptive scheduler could be left to
future work, but in testing any uneven runtime caused by the naive
task distribution seemed to only have a small effect on the total run
time, so the simplicity of the current solution is advantageous.

author: Jack Lovell <jacklovell1990@gmail.com>
commit message:
Build in parallel by default

When installing with pip or PyPA's `build` utility, , the `-j` option
for parallel builds is not passed by default. This increases the build
time on systems where wheels need to be built, e.g. for releases or
on systems where no pre-built wheel is available.

This commit introduces a modified `build_ext` command which by default
parallelises over all available CPUs, with an optional override using
the `RAYSECT_BUILD_JOBS` environment variable if for any reason the
number of build processes needs to be controlled manually.

author: Jack Lovell <jacklovell1990@gmail.com>
commit message:
Implement hybrid render engine

This render engine uses a combination of distributed and shared memory
tools to perform parallel rendering. MPI (mesage passing interface) is
used to communicate between processes with separate memory, for
example on different nodes of a compute cluster. Within each MPI
process a secondary render engine is used for shared memory
computation.

The secondary (or sub) render engine may be any other render
engine. `SerialEngine` and `MulticoreEngine` are currently supported,
though the former is less efficient than using the MPIEngine due to
additional IPC overhead. The engine+subengine architecture leaves room
to expand to additional engines in future, such as a
`MultiThreadEngine` in a free-threaded (no GIL) Python build.

Gathering of render results is done in the main process on MPI rank
0. A sub process is spawned on rank 0 in which the sub render engine
runs. For this to work efficiently the operating system must support
cheap process forking without memcopy. At present only Linux is known
to support this properly. MacOS may work if you're lucky. This
limitation means the render engine is not truly cross platform: if
cross-platform compatibility is required then SerialEngine and
MPIEngine are still the only suitable choices.

Ideally the result gathering and updates should not require spawning a
new process: a separate thread would make more logical sense. But
doing it in the same thread as the sub-engine is run causes resource
contention and therefore significant performance degradation.
Suggestions for fixing this would be most helpful.

Hybrid MPI+multiprocessing has many gotchas, and care must be taken
when launching the program especially with a job scheduler. The
documentation includes some hints about how the program should be run
with a few popular schedulers, and there is also a static helper
method for getting an appropriate number of processes for a parallel
sub worker. But ultimately it's the responsibility of the end user to
configure the engine and start the job properly: the render engine
itself does very little of this automatically.

2 new demos have been added showcasing this new render engine: one to
render the Raysect logo and one doing a high fidelity, multi-pass
adaptive sampling render of the Cornell Box.

commit message:
AGHQ and nimOptim (#1455)

* First major update to Laplace

Added caching of inner modes and hessian (cholesky).
Added an option to find MAPE instead of MLE within findMLE.
Updated inverse_negHess for when working at either last called parameter, or MLE to use cached values.
Added the same system for optimRandomEffects to fetch inner modes.

* Added AGHQ Grid Method

New file added "QuadratureGrids" to generate AGHQ grid. It will do all the sums that I need for the multivariate quadrature in the future.

* AGHQ added

both 1D and multivariate AGHQ added to basic function. General quadrature grid build function added as a new file.

Adding in gradients for 1D next.

* 1 dimension quadrature gradient added

Working for method 2. Need to tidy up method 1 and 3 now.

* gradients complete

basic check with beta binomial where Laplace is very wrong. Added a lot of nodes and converge to correct marginal log likelihood and gradient.

All 3 methods are now implemented.

* Access to transformations

Spectral or cholesky options for AGHQ.

* Updates as reviewing changes

Changed logic on when to cache the likelihood of the MLE/MAPE.

* Found a pesky couple of issues.

Cholesky was not being saved correctly in multivariate context. Fixed now.

Found a bug for memory exceeding in some quad grids. Need to put a setup fix in as well to make sure it's clean elsewhere.

* naming

_wrap was poor so just changed my intermediate function from negCholHess to negCholHessian as we are using negCholHess as a name of variable in code.

* expand info on Paul contribution in DESC

* add laplaceRpieces to Laplace.R.

This creates a list of R functions with shared closure in which compiled Laplace pieces are used but top-level control (outer and inner optimization) is run from R. This allows easy experimentation with different optimization methods.

* Minor updates

Started naming convention changes as discussed. Have not had time to complete.

* general capability to use arbitrary optim method through R via custom_optim

* remove debugging outputs from NimOptimProblem::calc_hessian

* Chasing Ghosts

Added some more details for checking convergence. Some tests needed there to see if it's practical.

Fixed naming convention in quadraturegrids

Ran Laplace tests. Some ghost issues there that I cannot recreate but end up with some very suspicious values for vcov sometimes.

Added tests for AGHQ. Identified bug for gradients. Resolved.

* order matters

Swapped definition order for saved_inner_negHess

* changing starting values

Updates for user control of starting values for inner optimization.

* Documentation

Added documentation to outer function. Further testing completed.

* Testing even grids

Figured grids should be allowed to be even at least. Reconfigured code to do that. Finding bugs. Not sure why with 80 grid points it blows up right now. Blows up for odd as well. Not sure what is going on for large grids...

* Not convinced

Working through testing. Beta-Binomial example needs lots of nodes. Need to work on it more.

* add nlminb support, optim extensibility, use nlminb by default in laplace, update tests

* Final tests

Updating tests and thresholds, created RTMB versions to compare aghq with.

* Tidying up updated version of Laplace

Adding documentation. Removed findMAP as discussed. Kept the posterior log density calculations for an advanced user to implement their own MAP calculations.

* fixing compiling errors

Spelling and ordering of code between versions was sloppy and hadn't checked compilation.

* recompute

For backwards compatibility I've added a "recompute" option so that when summary is called the inner optimization gets called again and avoids checking the cache.

* Testing

Had to update the indexing I did instead of loops for joint_logLik. Need to check later.

Passing Laplace tests.

* Test environment for initial values

Added test in ADlaplace for the different test inner initial values.

* cache and update model parameters

Cache change and update parameters
Changed optimize to have the option of parscale = "real" which is how it is called by findMLE

parameter values are not updated in model to MLE.

caching system can be switched on / off

* Removing helper for testing

Remove test env pointer to my workspace so that it can run generally.

* fix some tests and minor bugs

* going over tests and some hasty roxygen editing

* Add updateSettings. Revise roxygen.

* Clean up tests and details

* name typo AGQH

* fix test-ADlaplace crossed random effects

* register CALL_NimOptimProblem_[fn,gr,he]

* Laplace BFGS and roxygen entries. Remove one recent unnecessary change in C++

* add checkInterrupt and other tweaks to Laplace/AGHQ

* Fix syntax error.

* updates

to better handle possible cases like "3 - Inf".
Fix tests in light of use of checkLogProb.

Recreate gold files for trunc and dynamicIndexing testing for mcmc
tests that get different samples because of changes in number of random numbers generated.
